newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec, Ontario reach deal on construction workers.
newsitem.headline: Quebec, Ontario reach deal on construction workers.

text.p: The Quebec government said on Thursday that it had agreed to allow qualified construction workers and contractors from Ontario to do business in the province after Ontario threatened to retaliate.

The agreement in principle will let about 600 Ontario construction workers, mainly those based in the Ottawa-Hull area, to work in Quebec without having to obtain a permit from the province. The deal will exempt Ontario workers from having to submit to a qualifying exam in Quebec. Ontario workers will also be eligible to join a Quebec union and register with the provincial government agency.
Quebec Labour Minister Mathias Rioux told reporters that the government plans to introduce enabling legislation in the autumn session of the provincial parliament.
"We are both winners. This is progress in the relationship between Ontario and Quebec. We are not interested warring with Ontario, but with doing business," he said.

Rioux said Quebec is ready to sign similar agreeements with the other Canadian provinces. Cross-border trade in construction, particularly involving government contracts, has long been a contentious issue between Quebec and other provinces.
